name: Question 4
problem:
The standard matrix $T$ of a linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{3}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{3}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of $2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 5 & 7 & 9\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 17\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, we find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b],$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 5 & 7 & 9 & 17\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 5 & 7 & 9 & 17\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Hence, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. 
Now, from the second equation, we get 

$$
-{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1-2{x}_{3}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(1-2{x}_{3})+3{x}_{3}=4\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2+{x}_{3}.
$$

As a result, the general solution is given by 

$$
[\begin{aligned}2+{x}_{3} \\ 1-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=0,$ we have

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],
$$

where $T(x)=b.$

Finally, $2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2\cdot 2+1=5.$
